evidence.excerpt: Cloud providers offer preemptible compute instances at discounted prices, but tasks running on such instances may be interrupted when market demand rises above supply. This paper models a batch-processing workload that uses a mix of on-demand and preemptible instances as an M[X]/M/c queue with unreliable servers, where server failures correspond to preemption events governed by an exogenous price process modelled as a two-state continuous-time Markov chain. The stationary distribution is derived numerically using truncated state-space methods. A bidding strategy that sets the maximum acceptable spot price as a function of the remaining job deadline and estimated preemption rate is derived from the first-passage time distribution. Experiments use preemption rate estimates from a 30-day synthetic price series generated with parameters drawn from published empirical studies of spot markets. The bidding strategy achieves a 22 percent cost reduction over a fixed-bid baseline while maintaining deadline miss probability below 5 percent.
